OURS.seen: Own art derived from the kept north. No donor.

reply.image_seen: Image 1 compares four brown wooden ladder facings; image 2 shows a plated U-shaped south cap; image 3 shows two horizontal stringers joined by rounded rungs; image 4 shows the tall north ladder with broad plank rungs and crossed lashings; image 5 mirrors the east ladder; images 6 and 7 place these around a pit beside a human; image 8 enlarges the four wall placements.

concerns.evidence: East and west show rounded, dowel-like rungs between cylindrical stringers, whereas north has broad, flat plank rungs with conspicuous crossed lashings. The construction differs visibly. Apparent rung length alone is inconclusive because these views are foreshortened.

The south sprite and enlarged south-wall panel expose two substantial capped posts, their metal plates and lashings, and a full broad connecting plank. This reads as a shortened upper section of the north ladder rather than small tips with a glimpse of a rung.
All four isolated facings show wooden members, lashings and metal reinforcement plates. No pipe, hose or open bore is drawn, so there is no visible bore-plane violation.
The card specifies no ports, and the facings show no hose sockets, couplers or cords. The flat metal plates reinforce the wooden stringers; they do not depict connectors.
The wall panels show apparent placement against the pit, but no required assembled in-game capture is supplied. These composites cannot establish runtime draw-layer order or actual wall occlusion.
